concepts.learning_objective: Define learning as a relatively permanent change in behaviour or behavioural potential produced by experience.
Distinguish learning from temporary changes due to fatigue, habituation and drugs.
Explain that learning is an inferred process, different from observed performance.

topics.title: Classical Conditioning
topics.ncert_sections: Classical Conditioning; Determinants of Classical Conditioning

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the US, UR, CS and CR in Pavlov's experiment and everyday examples.
Compare simultaneous, delayed, trace and backward conditioning procedures.
Explain how appetitive or aversive US and the intensity of the CS affect conditioning.

topics.title: Operant/Instrumental Conditioning
topics.ncert_sections: Operant/Instrumental Conditioning; Determinants of Operant Conditioning; Box 5.1

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Skinner's operant conditioning and the nature of operants.
Distinguish positive reinforcement, negative reinforcement and punishment.
Explain how number, amount, quality, schedule and delay of reinforcement influence operant learning.
Distinguish primary and secondary reinforcers.
Explain extinction, resistance to extinction and spontaneous recovery.
Differentiate generalisation from discrimination and explain learned helplessness.
Explain observational learning using Bandura's Bobo doll study.
Describe Kohler's insight learning in chimpanzees.
Explain Tolman's latent learning and the idea of a cognitive map.
Describe paired-associates learning, serial learning and free recall.
Explain the determinants of verbal learning, including meaningfulness and the total time principle.
Explain category clustering and subjective organisation in free recall.

topics.title: Skill Learning and Factors Facilitating Learning

concepts.learning_objective: Identify Fitts' cognitive, associative and autonomous phases of skill acquisition.
Explain the partial reinforcement effect and the role of motivation in learning.
Explain preparedness for learning as a continuum set by biological constraints.
Describe the nature and origin of learning disabilities.
Identify the major symptoms of learning disabilities, including dyslexia.
